raw_glosses: (transitive) To give as a gift or donation.
glosses: To give as a gift or donation.

examples.text: Chelsea threw away two points when substitute Salomon Kalou gifted Valencia a penalty five minutes from time with a needless handball.
examples.ref: 2011 September 28, Jon Smith, “Valencia 1 - 1 Chelsea”, in BBC Sport:

examples.text: They drove on, every rise in the road lifting their sightline clear of the drystone dykes along the roadside, gifting glimpses of the firth and the islands, the blue peaks of Arran.

raw_glosses: (transitive) To give away, to concede easily.
glosses: To give away, to concede easily.

examples.text: Yet, a century later, what constitutes giftedness is still being debated. Some educators deny its existence entirely or say, with a roll of the eyes, that it is no more than a fantasy of pushy parents. Some take the view that all children have a particular gift of their own. Others conflate giftedness with talent when the two are often discrete: a gifted child may have been born with great potential but not have explored or displayed it. (Canadian psychologist Francoys Gagne is often cited for his theory that distinguishes giftedness from talent, offering explanations on how natural abilities can be developed into specific skills.)
examples.ref: 2023 November 3, Angus Holland, “‘I don’t think of it at all as a gift’: Why it’s complicated being a gifted child”, in The Sydney Morning Herald, Australia, archived from the original on 08 Sep 2025:

raw_glosses: (psychology) A psychological state associated with great intellectual ability and emotional sensitivity. There isn't a consensus over the characteristics of a gifted person or if it is a neurodivergence, with some completely denying its existence.
glosses: A psychological state associated with great intellectual ability and emotional sensitivity. There isn't a consensus over the characteristics of a gifted person or if it is a neurodivergence, with some completely denying its existence.

examples.text: I'll send you a GIF of the proposed logo.

raw_glosses: (computing) A bitmap image in a particular format with support for multiple images per file or animations, and up to 256 distinct colors per frame, including a fully transparent color.
glosses: A bitmap image in a particular format with support for multiple images per file or animations, and up to 256 distinct colors per frame, including a fully transparent color.

examples.text: Crying Dawson ruled the internet comment sections of the late ’00s and early ’10s. It’s “on the Mount Rushmore of GIFs,” says TV critic Sarah D. Bunting.
examples.ref: 2021 May 1, Constance Grady, quoting Sarah D. Bunting, “The Day Dawson Cried”, in Vox:

raw_glosses: (Internet slang, loosely) Any short video without audio, usually one which loops.
glosses: Any short video without audio, usually one which loops.

raw_glosses: (Internet, by extension) Any short video, in a format directly supported by HTML5 (ie. GIF, MP4, WebM)
glosses: Any short video, in a format directly supported by HTML5 (ie. GIF, MP4, WebM)
